title: LTS channel policy and cross-component compatibility matrix (runtime | API | SDKs | Console)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: define a clear LTS channel design and an explicit support/compatibility matrix that covers Redwood components: serving runtime, public API, official SDKs (JS/Python/Go), and Console. Scope includes: LTS naming and cadence, supported version windows per component, backward/forward compatibility rules, rollout gate definitions, and a plan for automated upgrade tooling + migration playbooks.

Motivation: customers (Dedicated/Private) require predictable support windows and upgrade guarantees. Engineering needs deterministic rollout gates and automated checks to reduce downgrade risk during fleet upgrades. This ticket produces the canonical policy and a support matrix artifact that will be referenced by release notes, onboarding docs, and the console upgrade UI.
acceptance_criteria: A human-readable support matrix that lists LTS channel name, semantic version ranges, and end-of-support dates for runtime, API, SDKs, and Console
Compatibility rules documented: which minor/patch combinations are supported across components and which require coordinated upgrades
Rollout gate checklist defined (smoke tests, canary %, regression evals, perf SLO validation, fallback policies)
Upgrade tooling requirements enumerated and scoped (canary automation, preflight validators, migration scripts, rollback steps)
Stakeholder sign-off from PM (Olivia Chen) and Security (Rajiv Mehta) recorded in comments
decisions: Adopt two LTS channels: Stable-LTS (24 months support, quarterly maintenance) and Maintenance-LTS (12 months support, critical fixes only)
Runtime LTS will be the primary gating dimension for client SDK and Console compatibility; API will maintain compatibility guarantees with two most recent runtime LTS releases
SDKs will follow semver but the LTS guarantee is limited to client compatibility with Stable-LTS for the supported major version; older patch-level SDKs supported for bug fixes only
Upgrades will be orchestrated via automated canary stages (1%, 10%, 50%, 100%) with a mandatory perf/regression evaluation step between each stage
Rollback must be automated for control-plane changes and documented for data-affecting changes; runtime binary rollbacks allowed within same major but require KV cache invalidation step
tasks: Draft canonical support matrix document and convert to JSON/CSV for console ingestion
Implement preflight validator to check API/Runtime version compatibility in deploy pipeline (CI)
Add rollout gate automation in deployment orchestrator to run perf SLO checks after each canary stage
Create SDK deprecation schedule pages and update npm/pypi package README with LTS mapping
Prepare console UX mocks for LTS selection and automated upgrade wizard (DES-321 for mock follow-up)
Run tabletop upgrade rehearsal for Dedicated customer scenario with Platform team

support_matrix: Stable-LTS (24 months): Runtime 2.0.x -> 2.5.x supported; API 2026.01 -> 2027.12; SDKs: JS 3.x, Python 2.x (compat shims); Console 5.x
Maintenance-LTS (12 months): Runtime 1.8.x -> 1.9.x; API 2025.07 -> 2026.06; SDKs: older patch-only fixes; Console 4.x (critical fixes only)
Compatibility rule A: API minor versions guaranteed to be compatible with the matching runtime LTS and one preceding LTS (two LTS window)
Compatibility rule B: SDKs are supported for the Stable-LTS major only; breaking changes must be exposed in SDK changelog and flagged in console upgrade UI
Compatibility rule C: Console will enforce a soft-check that warns admins when Managed runtime version is outside of supported matrix; auto-upgrade requires explicit admin opt-in
rollout_gates: Preflight: static validation (schema, version ranges, config flags) and security linting
Canary stages: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks and perf SLO verification between stages
Regression evals: run canonical prompt set against baseline and candidate; threshold: token-level quality delta < 0.5%
Operational checks: latency P95 and error-rate budgets must remain within 110% of baseline or gate fails
Post-upgrade: automated smoke jobs and audit log validation; final health check at 24h
